ideas.description: Calibrate the large-seed paired instrument. Nothing changes in the scored path. In an untimed side script, run the benchmark's own trial code (benchmark/ is not edited) on seeds 3-102 for two arms, one fresh process each. Arm A is unchanged E100 code (176e5ec). Arm B is E100 plus one math-neutral perturbation that does change fp bits: in prepare, compute the normalization as x*inv_std - mean*inv_std instead of (x-mean)*inv_std, which re-draws every seed's trajectory. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape). Free by-product for H4.5.1: in the same session, cluster the kernel-name sets already logged in E094/E098/E099/E106 against their process means. Store arm A's 100-seed vector as the paired baseline for every later large-seed A/B, so H8.2.2 needs only its treatment arm. Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged, which adds a 4th distinct scored sample.
ideas.expected: Scored row ~4.46-4.48 s, accuracy 0.751-0.756. Instrument: per-seed sd of the paired difference 0.3-0.5 pp, so the 100-seed SE is 0.03-0.05 pp, and the mean A-B difference stays within ±2 SE of 0. That sets the support/refute bar for H8.2.2, H12.x and H2.20 at ~2x the observed SE (~0.08 pp). If the paired-difference sd is <0.15 pp, seed pairing is strong and the 22-seed verdicts can stand. About 15-20 min of untimed GPU time.

ideas.description: Decisive test of bridge versus tail on the large-seed instrument. Run E108 code (340ecc1: 2@16 + 1.75@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.5@32 at bs 1024, everything else as E100) untimed through the benchmark trial code on seeds 3-102, one fresh process. Pair it per seed against the E100 vector from the H4.6.1 calibration run. Gate: run only after H4.6.1 has produced its baseline and SE. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 176e5ec. Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged, which adds another distinct gate sample (also useful to H4.8).
ideas.expected: No time change in the scored row (~4.47 s). Paired gain of E108 over E100: central estimate +0.03 to +0.08 pp (E108's 3-process off-seed was +0.09). If it is >= +0.08 pp (~2 SE), H8.2 is supported. The follow-up is then 2@16 + 2.0@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.25@32, judged on whether the bridge gain funds a ~1.5% net 32 px trim (target ~4.40 s). If it is <= -0.05 pp, H11 wins, H8.2 is refuted and bridge lengthening closes. Anything in between leaves both at ~0 and closes the reallocation axis as not worth it.

ideas.description: Late freeze of group 1 plus the stem as a FLOP/byte time lever, profiled untimed first. Step 1, untimed side script on E100 code: build a second static 32 px / bs-1024 train graph in which group 1's output is detached (no backward into group 1 or the stem; group-1 BN still runs in train mode). Warm it up in build. Measure ms/step and NVML energy over 20 steps for each variant, and project total run time for freezes over the last 15% and last 30% of samples. Step 2, only if the detached step is >=8% cheaper: score a freeze from 85% of samples, which lies inside the 32 px phase and covers the floor-hold and final EMA. From then on, group-1 filters drop out of the compiled Muon stacks (a second warmed variant of the update, with momentum untouched) and group-1 BN params drop out of the SGD foreach. Lookahead and the final EMA stay unchanged. Selection is a host-side flag, so nothing recompiles in timed code. Decide accuracy on the large-seed paired instrument (H4.6.1) against E100, plus two distinct scored samples.
ideas.expected: Profile: the detached step is 10-18% cheaper at 32 px. Group 1 works on the largest maps (31x31x128), so its backward conv plus elementwise work is a large share of the energy-bound step. Scored freeze from 85%: time -2.5 to -4% (about 4.29-4.36 s). Accuracy loss 0 to -0.1 pp paired, because group 1 barely moves at the floor LR. If the loss is <=0.1 pp, the rate is <=0.035 pp per 1%, it becomes the tip, and a 70% freeze is tried next. If the profiled saving is <6%, close H2.20 without a scored run. If the paired loss is >=0.15 pp, early layers still adapt at the end, as E093 suggests, and the line closes.

ideas.description: Gate-instrument question: is E100's seeds-0-2 advantage a persistent recipe x seed offset or luck? In an untimed side script that uses the benchmark's own trial code, run E100 (176e5ec) and E090 (48b13a7) on seeds 0-2 in 5 fresh processes each, alternating arms so time-of-day effects cancel. Log per-seed accuracy, per-seed final-weight checksums and kernel-name sets. The same data answers H4.7.1: compare the spread of the side-script E100 3-seed means with the distinct scored samples (0.7561/0.7516/0.7551). Scored row: rerun E100 unchanged.
ideas.expected: Scored row ~4.47 s, 0.751-0.756. Central prediction (luck): pooled E100 seeds-0-2 mean ~0.7530-0.7540 and pooled E100 - E090 within ±0.1 pp, converging toward their off-seed means. In that case the local gate passes ~50-60% of the time at zero population margin, and the next time cut needs ~+0.1 pp of accuracy funded first. If E100 - E090 is >= +0.15 pp on seeds 0-2 while off-seed stays ~0, the offset is persistent, and gate decisions should weight seeds 0-2 directly. For H4.7.1: if the side-script process sd of the 3-seed mean is <0.08 pp while scored samples spread 0.45 pp, the side script differs from the harness, and off-seed verdicts do not transfer to the gate.

structured_output.summary:
I added four ideas to the 4 already queued plus I122 (running), bringing the queue to 8. I dropped nothing: every queued idea's hypothesis is still open.

**The bottleneck is measurement, not ideas.** E100 sits at about 4.47 s with essentially no accuracy margin across seeds; its gate passes may be luck. Every recent difference is within about ±1 standard error (SE) at 22 seeds. So the top priority is calibrating the 100-seed paired comparison (I'm calling it the large-seed instrument) under H4.6.1:
- E100 against a math-neutral copy of itself on seeds 3-102.
- The same session analyses the cuDNN kernel-name logs that already exist, which H4.5.1 asks for.
- E100's 100-seed results become the baseline that later comparisons reuse.

**Two ideas follow the calibration run:**
- **H8.2.2 (bridge vs 32 px tail):** the decisive test. Run E108 on the same 100 seeds, paired against E100. It needs only the one new arm, because it reuses the calibration baseline.
- **H2.20.1 (late group-1 freeze):** the best remaining time lever that saves compute rather than per-step overhead. Group 1 works on the largest maps, so skipping its backward pass in the last ~15% of samples should save about 2.5-4% (target ~4.30-4.36 s). It gets an untimed profile first and is dropped if the detached step is less than 8% cheaper.

**H4.8.1:** runs E100 and E090 on seeds 0-2 in 5 fresh processes each. This settles whether E100's gate passes come from a lasting seed effect or from luck. The same data answers H4.7.1, which asks whether the side script behaves like the scored harness.

**What's left in the queue:**
- I114: depth cuts, profiled first. When it runs, it should be rebased from E090 onto E100.
- I123: group-3 width, starting with a free read of the kernel logs.
- I119: turning off translate late in training (H11).
- I124: multi-sample augmentation (H12.1, low prior).
- I122 (running): class-balanced batches.

The mix is roughly two-thirds exploit and one-third explore. I didn't queue any more scalar-knob variants (averaging strength, the Muon lr schedule shape, translate strength). Their predicted effects are below what we can measure today, so they should wait for the large-seed instrument.
